author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I am prepared to leave the data contracts without formal review for this specific cycle. We are skipping that layer of governance to ensure the acceptance criteria for the allocation logic receive full, strict sign off before the trucks leave. This trade off gives us the auditable guarantee we need for the committed pallets while we focus our limited review capacity on the core logic. The physical stock is already committed, so the audit trail for the decision making must be airtight, even if the upstream data validation remains informal for now. We are accepting the risk on the contracts to secure the final approval on the model behavior.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly identifies a compromise where formal data contract review is sacrificed to secure strict sign-off on the allocation logic, which the author states they are willing to accept losing in exchange for the core approval.
